payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:

# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the original blue mug from the source visibly positioned to the right of the headphones, visibly displaced toward them but short of that position, not displaced toward them, or is its identity or displacement unresolved?
node.criteria: Compare SOURCE and EDITED images, tracking the source light-blue mug by its shape, handle, appearance, and scene context. The endpoint is fully achieved only if that same mug is visibly positioned to the right of the headphones; a different mug on the right does not count. Incomplete fulfillment requires concrete visual evidence that the source mug itself was displaced toward the headphones, together with a visible remaining positional deficiency. Consider the blue blurred shape at the source mug’s former location and its spatial relation to the headphones and nearby mugs, but do not treat blur, color, or scene change alone as proof of movement. Evidence of no progress requires evidence that the source mug was not displaced toward the headphones, not merely failure to identify it at the endpoint. If identity or displacement cannot be determined from the visible continuity cues, report insufficient evidence rather than inferring either progress or no progress.
node.binding: SOURCE: the single light-blue mug left of the black headphones. EDITED: a blue blurred shape appears near the mug’s former location; a white mug is near the headphones and another white mug is to their right. Track the source mug using visible shape, handle, appearance, and context. Do not identify either white mug as the source mug without continuity evidence, and do not treat the blur alone as proof of displacement.
node.source_quote: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
node.aspect: Relative position and continuity of the source mug and headphones
node.endpoint: The mug is visibly positioned to the right of the headphones.
node.necessity: Moving the requested source mug, rather than introducing or repositioning a different mug, is necessary to fulfill the requested relative placement.
node.zero_when: There is evidence that the source blue mug was not displaced toward the right of the headphones. A different mug on the right does not count. If identity or displacement cannot be judged from the blur, candidate mugs, and other continuity cues, the evidence is insufficient rather than established zero fulfillment.
node.half_when: The source mug is not shown to have reached the right of the headphones, but concrete visual evidence supports that this same mug was displaced toward them; a specific remaining positional deficiency is visible. A blur alone, without evidence connecting it to displacement of the source mug, is insufficient.
node.full_when: The source blue mug is visibly identifiable as the same mug and is positioned to the right of the headphones in the edited image.

node_traces.evidence: The source light-blue mug is clearly left of the headphones. In the edited image, a blue blurred shape remains near its former location, while two white mugs appear near and to the right of the headphones. Neither white mug has visible continuity with the source mug, and the blur does not establish that the source mug itself moved toward the headphones. Thus its identity or displacement cannot be determined from the visible evidence.

Do not infer that the blur is the moved mug or count a replacement mug as progress. Instead, explicitly assess whether the blur’s position/shape and the changed scene provide concrete evidence of displacement toward the headphones, and whether a remaining positional deficiency is visible. If they do not establish movement of the source mug, retain unresolved rather than forcing partial or zero. Keep confidence calibrated to that distinction; the high-confidence unknown currently yields no coverage, so make the evidence-to-status criterion explicit without treating the reference label as atomic ground truth."}
